bug_semantics: IncomingRequest::isSecure() accepted client-controlled X-Forwarded-Proto: https and Front-End-Https values without first establishing that REMOTE_ADDR was a configured trusted proxy, so an HTTP request could be misclassified as secure and bypass HTTPS-dependent application decisions in exposed deployments.
flaw_origin: d0c35d680a38e10db4162bf2610ed1734834cb59 first added isSecure() to system/HTTPLite/IncomingRequest.php with an unconditional HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO trust branch; its parent had no isSecure() implementation. 6e372fd91e618ba52ee45456bd16050a0c35d615 later retained that branch and added the equally unguarded HTTP_FRONT_END_HTTPS branch. Later API, Rector, whitespace, and brace rewrites preserved rather than originated the trust flaw.
ai_marker: No AI marker appears in the BIC metadata or message; the same human author and committer, Lonnie Ezell, created it on 2015-10-23, before modern generative coding assistants.
evidence: The PUBLISHED CVE record and vendor GHSA agree that versions below 4.7.4 trust X-Forwarded-Proto and Front-End-Https from arbitrary requests and that 4.7.4 fixes the issue.

git show d0c35d680a38e10db4162bf2610ed1734834cb59 adds isSecure() and its unconditional HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO == https branch; parent 1d95a359f8297f34180576ade5ea04e0eb52e7e4 contains neither isSecure nor that branch.
git show 6e372fd91e618ba52ee45456bd16050a0c35d615 adds the unconditional HTTP_FRONT_END_HTTPS branch while retaining forwarded-proto trust, closing the second advisory mechanism.

git show ecbf044666bed41d23f07518096d9843fe6c08b0 adds an early false return when isFromTrustedProxy() fails before evaluating both forwarding headers; its parent 72476b3aaad3ccd72921dcab67b0db6484741d0a lacks that guard.

Local topology places the BIC in v4.7.3 and v4.7.4, excludes the fix from v4.7.3, and includes it in v4.7.4; local tag targets are 723162211eb3c17f222f943c4610311dcf9167f1 and 2bd0f01d2813f9ec06db42643ce39d9f5428bf6d.
reasoning: The first surviving project commit that creates the vulnerable source-to-sink is d0c35d680a38e10db4162bf2610ed1734834cb59: attacker-controlled forwarded-proto reaches isSecure()'s true return without proxy authentication, and the immediate parent lacks the method. The later Front-End-Https addition is a second instance of the same missing trust boundary, while subsequent blamed commits are transformations. The direct fix inserts one shared trusted-proxy gate before both sinks. The 2015 BIC has no AI marker and predates modern generative coding assistants, so the real vulnerability is human-authored.
